newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: SABIC says Q1 net falls 5.6 percent.
newsitem.headline: SABIC says Q1 net falls 5.6 percent.

text.p: Saudi Arabia's industrial giant Saudi Basic Industries Corp (SABIC) said on Tuesday its net profit for the first quarter of 1997 fell 5.6 percent to 1.08 billion riyals.
A company statement said this compared to net profits of 1.15 billion riyals at end-March 1996.
Saudi Industry and Electricity Minister Hashem bin Abdullah bin Hashem Yamani attributed the drop to a fall in world prices, despite increased SABIC output. Yamani is SABIC's chairman.

Vice chairman and managing director Ibrahim Bin Salameh said SABIC's total output in the first three months of 1997 reached 5.640 million tonnes compared with 5.616 million tonnes in the same period last year.
First quarter sales were 4.386 million tonnes compared to 4.399 million tonnes.

He said increased production in the first quarter was because many expansion projects had come on stream while other projects were proceeding as scheduled in line with SABIC's plan to increase total annual production to 28 million tonnes by the year 2000.
SABIC is 70-percent owned by the Saudi government.
